title: Singly exponential shortest solutions of word equations
formal: Is there a polynomial p such that every satisfiable word equation \(u=v\) of length \(n=length(u)+length(v)\), over a finite constant alphabet and variables, admits a solution replacing each variable by a word of length at most \(2^{p(n)}\)?
context:
Solutions are free-monoid substitutions fixing the constants, and may use the empty word. The polynomial p must be independent of the equation. This is the singly exponential solution-length question; no sharper linear exponent is asserted. Such a bound would imply membership in NP, but the converse is not claimed.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Would bound the hidden size of solutions and support efficient compressed certificates for a central string-constraint problem.
